comments.author: @jondevaney6860
comments.text:
Geoff, the central message of your video is the term "ecumene." I learned this in high school geography class (in Toronto, back in the 1970s) - a teacher explained how the population ecumene (settled area) of Canada was strung out along the southern boundary, forming what is in effect a long narrow country (a bit similar to Chile, in a vague way).

A key point of Canadian geography theory is nodes versus "hinterlands." Nodes are the cities and towns, and they are surrounded, at large scales, by hinterlands, fairly empty 'frontier' areas and wilderness (used for resource extraction and tiny settlements like Indian reserves). This is important to understanding how Canada works.
